definition: Value at Risk estimates a threshold loss over a target horizon at a chosen confidence level.
implication: Use it as a compact tail-loss reference, not as a worst-case bound.

definition: Expected Shortfall measures the average loss beyond the VaR cutoff and is more sensitive to extreme tails.
implication: Escalate when ES rises faster than VaR because downside tails are thickening.

definition: Max drawdown measures the peak-to-trough decline over the selected window.
implication: Large drawdowns matter when a signal suggests trend failure rather than noise.

definition: A volatility regime reflects the current intensity and persistence of realized price fluctuations.
implication: High realized volatility can turn a tactical signal into a portfolio-risk event.

definition: Correlation break tracks how quickly an asset's linkage to a benchmark shifts.
implication: A sharp jump can signal broader de-risking instead of asset-specific stress.
